ack-twins-swap.claim: defendant A (claim): the negotiation automaton is initiator/responder symmetric at the Ack twins -- Ack-Rcvd and Ack-Sent are the two one-step-from-Open states, and sec.4.2 describes them in near-verbatim mirror sentences: 'Ack-Received': 'a Configure-Request has been sent and a Configure-Ack has been received. The Restart timer is still running, since a Configure-Ack has not yet been sent' (snapshot txt:945-949) vs 'Ack-Sent': 'a Configure-Request and a Configure-Ack have both been sent, but a Configure-Ack has not yet been received. The Restart timer is running' (snapshot txt:951-956) -- so swapping states 7 <-> 8 with every other state fixed should map the negotiation race onto itself.

closing-stopping-swap.claim: defendant B: Closing and Stopping are the termination twins -- in both, a Terminate-Request has been sent and the Restart timer is running while waiting for a Terminate-Ack, and sec.4.2 says 'The Stopping state is the Open counterpart to the Closing state' (snapshot txt:918-929, counterpart sentence at txt:920; 'Closing' at txt:906-916), so maybe states 4 <-> 5 can be swapped alone

closed-stopped-swap.claim: defendant C: Closed and Stopped are the quiet twins -- in neither is a negotiation in flight, in neither does the Restart timer run, and both answer an unwanted Configure-Request with a Terminate-Ack (sec.4.2 'Closed' txt:853-860, 'Stopped' txt:862-872; txt:864 'The Stopped state is the Open counterpart to the Closed state'), so maybe states 2 <-> 3 can be swapped alone

pads.claim: positive control: padding states 10 and 11 have byte-identical rows (every event self-loops, reward 0), so the swap is a genuine symmetry under BOTH readings and should be admitted everywhere
